messages:
mira: Heads-up: starting 2026-04-01 were deprecating long-lived org service accounts. New policy requires scoped delegation tokens (short-lived OAuth clients) for all runtime and CI access. This reduces blast radius after credential compromise. Rollout window: 2026-04-01 -> 2026-04-14. See migration steps below.

alina: Is this mandatory for sandbox and staging too or only prod infra?

mira: Mandatory for all environments. Exceptions are temporary and must be requested via the migration form.

paul: TL;DR for CI: do we swap service account creds for client credentials in CI secrets? Any breaking changes?

ken: For supported runners well replace secrets with DELEGATION_CLIENT_ID and DELEGATION_CLIENT_SECRET and wire token exchange in the runner image. Were providing a GH Actions composite action and a Koios runner shim. Custom runners require you to call token-exchange before doing anything that uses the token.

sam: Example for GH Actions:

```yaml
- name: Exchange delegated token
  uses: redwood-security/token-exchange@v1
  with:
    client_id: ${{ secrets.DELEGATION_CLIENT_ID }}
    client_secret: ${{ secrets.DELEGATION_CLIENT_SECRET }}
- name: Use token
  run: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ${{ steps.token.outputs.access_token }}" https://artifact.redwood/upload
```

mira: Migration steps (short):
1) Run scanner: migration-lint scan --org <org> (lists services using long-lived accounts).
2) For each service: create scoped client via token-refactorer CLI or Console (recommend scope minimal perms).
3) Swap env/secret to DELEGATION_CLIENT_ID/SECRET and update runtime to call token-exchange.
4) Enable token introspection policy in runtime.
5) Mark migration complete in the console.

devops-oncall: We will run an automation to open PRs for common repo patterns:
- Dry run: 2026-04-01 03:00 UTC (PRs in draft).
- Apply: 2026-04-03 05:00 UTC (auto-merge to allow opt-out).
- Enforcement: 2026-04-08 00:00 UTC (runtimes will start rejecting broad service account usage).

paul: If an auto-change breaks deploys, what's the rollback?

mira: We have a 48h fallback window after a change where the old service account is still usable but flagged in audit logs. Use the migration console to request emergency rollback; exceptions tracked.

alina: How long are tokens valid? Some batch jobs run for hours.

ken: Default TTL is 1h. For long-running batch jobs, request extended TTL (up to 12h) through the migration form with justification. Well approve only when the job cannot be re-architected.

security-bot: Audit snapshot for team infra-tools: scanned 2026-03-29T12:10Z, 9 services with long-lived creds, 4 auto-PRs opened, 0 exceptions granted. Dashboard: https://console.redwood/migrations/infra-tools

sam: Any breaking changes to AAD/GCP/OIDC integrations?

mira: No vendor changes required. Token-refactorer issues delegated OAuth clients that map to provider identities. You may need to update provider config to accept the new client IDs for federation. See provider-specific docs in the migration FAQ.

paul: Will there be k8s sidecar support for token refresh?

ken: Yes: recommended path is the token-sidecar (Helm chart) that fetches/refreshes tokens and writes them to a projected volume. Well publish the chart and an example k8s deployment by 2026-03-31.

alina: Where do we log exceptions and request extended TTLs?

mira: migration form & exception tracker: https://intranet.redwood/eng/security/delegation-exceptions. Include owner, justification, mitigation, and estimated sunset date.

devops-oncall: Action items for teams: 
- Run migration-lint and review results (by 2026-03-30).
- Opt-in to automation or provide repo exclusions (by 2026-03-31).
- Replace secrets in CI and runtimes during rollout window (2026-04-01 -> 2026-04-14).

mira: If youre unsure how to proceed, ping #eng-security or DM me. Were scheduling two office hours (2026-03-30 16:00 UTC, 2026-03-31 09:00 UTC) to help with migrations.

alina: Thanks, will run the scanner and add my repos to the opt-in list.

mira: Appreciate it. This is a high-impact change but lowers risk a lot long-term. :lock: :white_check_mark:
